Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

lay it on thick phrase

also you’re putting it on a little thick, overdo it, exaggerate, don’t exaggerate

classical

Cic. Fam. 7.5.3 (Lewis & Short: “of discourse, rather more tedious or troublesome”)
Traupman 106: you’re putting it on a little thick, es pūtidiusculus

pūtidiusculus, pūtidiuscula, pūtidiusculum

adjective, diminutive of the comparative of pūtidus, declension

rather tiresome, a bit over the top (of talk)

From pūtidus, rotten, hence of style “affected, overdone”. The word is Cicero’s, from a letter, and rare.

Examples

  • Nōlī omnia in mājus extollere!

    Don’t exaggerate everything!Traupman 311

SourcesLewis & Short: putidiusculus

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 106, 311.
